text: package exports six functions, file R/: functions follow interface conventions: accept model object, optional display flags (showConf, showGrid, showSusp), axis labels, color parameters. return plotly object.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: plotly_alt plotly_rel require fully-fitted alt object WeibullR.ALT. three-step pipeline alt.make() → alt.parallel() → alt.fit(). plotly_alt requires minimum alt.parallel() (needs $parallel_par); plotly_rel additionally requires alt.fit() (needs $alt_coef). functions internally call WeibullR::wblr() compute empirical plotting positions raw $data entries.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: plotly_wblr, plotly_rga, plotly_contour accept either single model object list objects. plotly_alt handles multiple stress levels one alt object using internal loop (list API). list provided: - object rendered distinct color 10-color default palette (palette across three functions). - cols parameter accepts explicit color vector, recycled match number objects. - single objects, existing per-element color params (probCol, fitCol, confCol, etc.) still apply. - plotly_wblr requires objects share distribution type ignores susp (warning) multiple objects passed. - plot built initializing empty plot_ly() looping objects, appending traces . single layout() call applied loop. - legendgroup set per object clicking legend entry toggles traces object.

title: CLAUDE.md
text: complex function (376 lines). Key details: - Weibull plots use log scale y-axis custom tick marks probability percentiles; lognormal plots use qnorm (linear scale). - Supports 2-parameter 3-parameter Weibull (dist='weibull3p'). - suspension data passed via susp, subplot added main plot. - Interval censored data ($interval_data) extracted plotted separately. - Confidence bounds use toRGB() alpha 0.2 semi-transparent fills. - Goodness--fit shown via R² (rank regression) log-likelihood (MLE).

title: ReliaPlotR
text: build probability plot, first fit wblr object using WeibullR package use plotly_wblr build plot.  build contour plot, use plotly_contour function. Note contour plots available method.fit='mle' method.conf='lrb'.

title: Accelerated Life Testing (ALT)
text: WeibullR.ALT package uses three-step pipeline create ALT model. Step 1 — Create data sets stress level using alt.data(): Step 2 — Fit parallel models across stress levels using alt.make() alt.parallel(): Step 3 — Fit life-stress relationship using alt.fit():
code: d1 <- alt.data(c(248, 456, 528, 731, 813, 537), stress = 300) d2 <- alt.data(c(164, 176, 289), stress = 350) d3 <- alt.data(c(88, 112, 152), stress = 400) obj <- alt.parallel(   alt.make(list(d1, d2, d3), dist = "weibull", alt.model = "arrhenius", view_dist_fits = FALSE),   view_parallel_fits = FALSE ) obj <- alt.fit(obj)

title: Accelerated Life Testing (ALT)
text: plotly_alt() overlays one probability-paper fit line per stress level. Data points show empirical plotting positions; lines show theoretical Weibull (lognormal) fit. Click legend entry toggle stress level .
code: plotly_alt(obj)

title: Accelerated Life Testing (ALT)
text: plot accepts several optional arguments:
code: plotly_alt(   obj,   main    = "Reliability Test Results",   xlab    = "Hours to Failure",   cols    = c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c"),   showGrid = FALSE )

title: Accelerated Life Testing (ALT)
text: plotly_rel() displays characteristic life (eta Weibull, median life lognormal) changes stress level, along fitted Arrhenius Power Law relationship. plot includes: Points (×) — characteristic-life estimates parallel fits stress level Red line — fitted life-stress relationship (Arrhenius Power Law) Dashed blue lines — percentile bands (10th 90th default)
code: plotly_rel(obj)

text: Use percentiles argument change percentile bands shown:
code: plotly_rel(obj, percentiles = c(5, 50, 95))

title: Repairable Systems Analysis
text: Mean Cumulative Function (MCF) non-parametric estimate expected cumulative number failures per system time t. computed using Nelson-Aalen estimator, accounts systems still operating (censored) end observation window. shaded band shows pointwise confidence interval. Hover step function read exact MCF values event time.
code: end_times <- c(U1 = 600, U2 = 600, U3 = 600, U4 = 600, U5 = 600) fit_mcf   <- mcf(id = id, time = time, end_time = end_times) plotly_mcf(fit_mcf)

title: Repairable Systems Analysis
text: exposure plot tracks cumulative event rate — total failures divided total system-time — observation period. rising rate indicates deteriorating fleet; flat falling rate indicates stability improvement.
code: fit_exp <- exposure(id = id, time = time) plotly_exposure(fit_exp)

title: Repairable Systems Analysis
text: Non-Homogeneous Poisson Process (NHPP) fits parametric model recurrent failure process. Power Law model (also called Crow-AMSAA model repairable systems) describes failure intensity changes time: λ(t)=λβtβ−1\lambda(t) = \lambda \beta \, t^{\beta - 1} shape parameter β<1\beta < 1 indicates reliability improvement; β>1\beta > 1 indicates deterioration; β=1\beta = 1 reduces homogeneous Poisson process.
code: times  <- c(120, 200, 310, 370, 430, 480, 490, 560) events <- c(  1,   1,   1,   1,   1,   1,   1,   1) fit_nhpp <- nhpp(time = times, event = events, model_type = "Power Law") plotly_nhpp(fit_nhpp)

title: Repairable Systems Analysis
text: corrective action design change introduced mid-program, failure process may shift. piecewise NHPP fits separate Power Law segments either side specified breakpoint, shown vertical dotted line:
code: # Dense failures before the design change (t < 500), sparse afterwards times2  <- c(30, 65, 105, 150, 200, 255, 315, 380, 450, 800, 1300, 1950, 2800) events2 <- rep(1, 13) fit_nhpp2 <- nhpp(time = times2, event = events2, breaks = 500, method = "LS") plotly_nhpp(fit_nhpp2, fitCol = "steelblue", confCol = "steelblue", breakCol = "red")

title: Repairable Systems Analysis
text: Multiple MCF NHPP estimates can overlaid plot passing list objects. useful comparing two fleets, two time periods, /scenario.
code: id2   <- c("A","A","B","B","B","C") time2 <- c(180, 420, 90, 310, 530, 260) end2  <- c(A = 600, B = 600, C = 600) fit_mcf2 <- mcf(id = id2, time = time2, end_time = end2)  plotly_mcf(list(fit_mcf, fit_mcf2), cols = c("steelblue", "tomato"))

title: Life Data Analysis

title: Life Data Analysis
text: create interval censored model, let’s use inspection data Silkworth, 2020. add suspension data units surviving last inspection date. Finally, add fit plot results.
code: inspection_data <- data.frame(   left = c(0, 6.12, 19.92, 29.64, 35.4, 39.72, 45.32, 52.32),   right = c(6.12, 19.92, 29.64, 35.4, 39.72, 45.32, 52.32, 63.48),   qty = c(5, 16, 12, 18, 18, 2, 6, 17) ) suspensions <- data.frame(time = 63.48, event = 0, qty = 73) obj <- wblr(suspensions, interval = inspection_data) obj <- wblr.fit(obj, method.fit = "mle") obj <- wblr.conf(obj, method.conf = "fm", lty = 2) suspensions <- as.vector(suspensions$time) plotly_wblr(obj,   susp = suspensions, fitCol = "red", confCol = "red", intCol = "blue",   main = "Parts Cracking Inspection Interval Analysis",   ylab = "Cumulative % Cracked", xlab = "Inspection Time" )

title: Interactive Reliability Growth Plot. — plotly_rga
text: Crow-AMSAA (NHPP Power Law) model fits Non-Homogeneous Poisson Process expected cumulative failures follow \(E[N(t)] = \lambda t^\beta\). \(\beta < 1\) indicates reliability growth (decreasing failure rate), \(\beta > 1\) indicates reliability degradation. piecewise models, separate set parameters fit within interval defined breaks, vertical lines mark change-point times.

title: Interactive Probability Plot. — plotly_wblr
text: function creates interactive probability plot one wblr objects. list objects provided models overlaid plot, rendered distinct color. objects must use distribution family. can include confidence bounds, suspension data (single object ), results table.

title: Interactive Probability Plot. — plotly_wblr
code: plotly_wblr(   wblr_obj,   susp = NULL,   showConf = TRUE,   showSusp = TRUE,   showGrid = TRUE,   main = "Probability Plot",   xlab = "Time to Failure",   ylab = "Probability",   probCol = "black",   fitCol = "black",   confCol = "black",   intCol = "black",   gridCol = "lightgray",   signif = 3,   cols = NULL )

title: Interactive Probability Plot. — plotly_wblr
text: wblr_obj single object class 'wblr', list objects. required argument. object must use distribution (e.g. Weibull lognormal). Suspension subplots shown single object provided. susp optional numeric vector suspension data. Default NULL. Ignored multiple wblr objects provided. showConf Show confidence bounds (TRUE) (FALSE). Default TRUE confidence bounds available wblr object. showSusp Show suspensions plot (TRUE) (FALSE). Default TRUE susp provided. showGrid Show grid (TRUE) hide grid (FALSE). Default TRUE. main Main title. Default 'Probability Plot'. xlab X-axis label. Default 'Time Failure'. ylab Y-axis label. Default 'Probability'. probCol Color probability values. Default 'black'. Used single wblr object; ignored `cols` provided multiple objects supplied. fitCol Color model fit. Default 'black'. Used single wblr object; ignored `cols` provided multiple objects supplied. confCol Color confidence bounds. Default 'black'. Used single wblr object; ignored `cols` provided multiple objects supplied. intCol Color intervals interval censored models. Default 'black'. gridCol Color grid. Default 'lightgray'. signif Significant digits results. Default 3. Must positive integer. cols Optional character vector colors, one per wblr object. provided, object's data points, fit line, confidence bounds drawn corresponding color. Recycled shorter number objects.

title: Interactive Probability Plot. — plotly_wblr
text: Weibull distributions y-axis uses double-log transformation (log(-log(1 - F))) straight line represents perfect Weibull fit. lognormal distributions y-axis uses normal quantile transformation (qnorm(F)), .e., standard normal probability paper. Three-parameter Weibull (dist = 'weibull3p') shifts x-axis estimated location (gamma) parameter applying transformation. Goodness--fit reported R² rank-regression fits log-likelihood MLE fits.
